clue.text: Reportedly bestow the title of 'sir' on Picaroon? Time to party till dawn!

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to give someone a knighthood is to make a knight of them
the setter, Picaroon, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter imagines being knighted and declares it a reason to celebrate all night.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first part is heard: MAKE A KNIGHT OF sounds like MAKE A NIGHT OF; then I (the setter) and T (time) are added in plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to spend a whole evening celebrating, carrying on into the small hours.

clue.text: Single quantity of DNA that I'm allocated?

definitions.text: Single quantity of DNA that I'm allocated?

parts.words: Single quantity of DNA that I'm allocated?
parts.note: read the answer as three words: a possessive, a unit of heredity and a measured share

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MY GENE RATION: my own allotted portion of genetic material. Read as normal it is the people born around the same time as me, and a famous song by the Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the phrase means one's own age group, the people born in the same era as oneself.

clue.text: Thousands round hotel area head for interior shade

indicators.note: round means the pair of letters goes around the next pieces

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so two of them for thousands
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: head for means take the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is choosing a paint colour for the inside of a large hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a dull yellowish-brown colour, a shade familiar from military uniforms.

clue.text: Winging it in promo, politician to throw away £1,000

parts.note: a promo is an advertisement, an ad
a Lib is a Liberal politician
to bin something is to throw it away
a grand is a thousand pounds, abbreviated G

explanation.surface: A politician improvises during a promotional event and squanders a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: To bin is British slang for throwing in the rubbish; a grand (G) is a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad-libbing is speaking or performing without preparation, improvising as one goes along.

clue.text: Out of school holidays, engaging one caretaker

indicators.note: engaging means holding the next piece inside, as an employer takes someone on

parts.note: when it is not the holidays, pupils are in term
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A school hires someone to look after the building during term time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caretaker' looks like a school janitor, but it is used as an adjective, as in a caretaker government.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim or caretaker leader holds office temporarily until a permanent replacement is found.

clue.text: Almost home, not from South American city

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a house is a home

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the word is turned round

explanation.surface: A traveller is nearly home but is not coming from South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American city' reads as one phrase; the clue breaks it, with 'from South' as the upward-reading signal on NOT, making TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Houston is a large city in Texas, home of NASA's mission control.

clue.text: The Parisian punching couple around hooter

indicators.note: punching means driving into the middle of the other piece
around here means turned about, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a couple is two
le is French for the, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A Frenchman punches two people over a car horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn or a nose, but here it is a bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, and owls are known for their hooting call.

clue.text: List what fibbers do endlessly, one such as Boris

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: liars invent stories
Boris Johnson is a Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A political jibe listing a prime minister among habitual liars.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris is Boris Johnson, the former Conservative (Tory) Prime Minister of the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete itemised record of goods or possessions, a catalogue.

clue.text: Sought-after item from good pork pie manufacturer returned

indicators.note: returned means the word is sent back, reading in reverse

parts.note: pork pie is rhyming slang for lie, so its maker is a liar

explanation.surface: A prized product from a reputable maker of pork pies is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang a pork pie (often 'porky') is a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A grail, after the Holy Grail of legend, is anything eagerly pursued or desired.

clue.text: The one rule broken in rigged vote

indicators.note: in means the second jumble sits inside the first
a rigged vote is tampered with, so its letters are rearranged
a broken rule is bent out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An election is fixed, so a regulation gets broken in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The one' looks like an article and a number, but it is the romantic sense of a person's destined partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A true love is the person one is meant to be with, a soulmate.

clue.text: Character blocking ball by old footballer in decline

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, inside the other piece

parts.note: in football, a ball played to a teammate is a pass
character can mean tone, the general quality or feel of something
George Best was a famous Manchester United and Northern Ireland footballer

explanation.surface: A tough opponent blocks a pass from an ageing football star who is losing his touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past their best is no longer at the peak of their abilities, in decline.

clue.text: After new trouble, save digital enhancements here

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
save means except, as does bar

explanation.surface: After fresh difficulties, someone saves files with digital improvements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digital' suggests computers, but it refers to fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail bar is a salon where fingernails are manicured and decorated.

clue.text: Answer on most of epic Faerie Queen

indicators.note: on means the A is added after the other piece
most of means the final letter is removed

parts.note: Titanic is an epic film by James Cameron

explanation.surface: A solver writes an answer on most of Spenser's epic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Spenser's Faerie Queene, but Titania is the fairy queen of A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's comedy, wife of Oberon.

clue.text: Scholar in fresh air catching bees

indicators.note: catching means holding the next piece inside
fresh means newly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letter B spelt out is bee, so bees are BB

explanation.surface: A scholar out in the open air gets caught up with bees.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish teacher learned in religious law, a religious scholar.

clue.text: Trouble right behind English in Second Division

indicators.note: behind means the R comes after the rest
in means the E sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: B is second, as in B-grade
a football division is a league

explanation.surface: A football club runs into difficulty in a lower division.
explanation.definitionFit: To beleaguer is to beset or harass persistently, as a besieging army does.

clue.text: On isle, leave healthy food

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits on top of the next, so comes first

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea
to get out is to leave

explanation.surface: On an island, someone abandons their healthy diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangetout are flat pea pods eaten whole, a green vegetable.

clue.text: Supply airlifted for end of fast festivity

indicators.note: supply is read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Supplies are flown in for a celebration marking the end of a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb about provisions; read as 'supplely' it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eid al-Fitr is the Muslim festival celebrating the close of Ramadan's month of fasting.

clue.text: Appealing on set or stage, entice running around

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters enclose the next piece
running means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a stage of a journey is a leg

explanation.surface: An actor attractive on screen or in the theatre lures people in.
explanation.definitionFit: Telegenic describes someone who looks good on television, attractive on camera.

clue.text: Newspaper's lead article has sharp material

indicators.note: lead means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
keen can mean sharp, as of a blade

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead story has a pointed edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing, a type of fabric.

clue.text: Tries to win over bowlers, say, in competition

indicators.note: in means the hats sit inside the other piece

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
a bowler is a kind of hat, so bowlers are an example of hats

explanation.surface: A cricket team tries to win over its bowlers during a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowlers' suggests cricket, but they are hats.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat someone up is to talk flirtatiously to them, hoping to attract them.

clue.text: Elder statesman from Germany with zero cash abroad

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
O looks like zero
the yen is a foreign currency, Japan's

explanation.surface: A senior politician from Germany finds himself with no money abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior or respected member of a group, its revered veteran.

clue.text: Acclaim novel method when scrubbing inn

indicators.note: scrubbing means deleting, so the inn is taken away

parts.note: an innovation is a new method

explanation.surface: A new way of cleaning a pub wins applause.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause, public acclaim for a performance.

clue.text: What Asian banks hold from half of factories etc

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the word's letters are taken

parts.note: factories and the like make up industries

explanation.surface: Asian banks hold half of their investments in factories and similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests money, but they are riverbanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a major river of Pakistan, flowing between its banks.

clue.text: Claims member tucked into alcoholic drinks

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: ales are alcoholic drinks
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A club member settles down with some beers, making assertions.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert something without proof, so alleges means asserts.

clue.text: Judge, say, goes north round part of the summer

indicators.note: round means enclosing the next piece
in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, which say also means
August, AUG, is a summer month

explanation.surface: A judge, for instance, heads north for a summer break.
explanation.definitionFit: To gauge is to estimate or assess, which is what judging something means.

clue.text: What female tanner may put on small strip

definitions.text: What female tanner may put on

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A sunbather pulls on a tiny bikini.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundress is a light, sleeveless summer dress worn in hot weather by someone sunbathing.

clue.text: Harden cover son's left out

indicators.note: left out means removed from the word

parts.note: to insure is to provide cover
S is the standard abbreviation for son; the 's is the verb is

explanation.surface: A son is not included in an insurance policy, so the family must toughen up.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure someone is to accustom them to hardship until they become tough.

clue.text: Perhaps have received ideal offer at first

indicators.note: at first means this piece comes before the other

parts.note: to present is to offer
something perfect is ideal

explanation.surface: Someone says they may have got a great proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have received' is an example of the grammar tense, hence 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: The present perfect is the verb tense formed with have plus a past participle, as in that phrase.
